extracted.intended_audience: international patent applicants and representatives entering the European phase (EPO) under the PCT
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and documentary requirements and options for applicants entering the European (EPO) regional phase from an international (PCT) application, including Form 1200 entries, translations, fees, amendments, biological material and sequence listings, acceleration options and payment methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond to communication (Rule 161(1) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to respond in due time to a communication will lead to the application being deemed to be withdrawn (Rule 161(1) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments and/or comments filed on entry into the regional phase may be considered to constitute a response to the WO‑ISA, IPER or SISR if the applicant indicates on Form 1200 that such amendments/comments are to form the basis for further prosecution. Amendments under Article 19 and/or 34 PCT filed in the international phase and maintained on entry may constitute a response subject to certain requirements (see Guidelines C‑III,2.2 and E‑IX,3). The applicant must clearly indicate which documents are to form the basis for further prosecution by crossing the appropriate boxes in section 6.1 or 6.2 of Form 1200 and list them in the table on page 8; exceptional circumstances should be explained on an additional sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six‑month amendment period after communication (Rule 161 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant can amend the application at any time within a non‑extendable period of six months from the communication (Forms 1226AA, 1226BB, 1226CC) under Rule 161(1) and (2) EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This six‑month period is non‑extendable. Pages of amendments filed during this six‑month period under Rule 161 EPC are not taken into account in the calculation of the additional fee as part of the filing fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page fee treatment for amendments filed within six months
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages of amendments filed during the six‑month period under Rule 161 EPC are not taken into account in the calculation of the additional fee as part of the filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, if amendments filed at this stage reduce the number of pages already paid for, no refund of the additional fee will be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handwritten amendments on entry
rubrics_metrics.description: If application documents filed on entry into the European phase contain handwritten amendments, the EPO will issue an invitation to remedy this deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of non‑compliance with the invitation to remedy handwritten amendments, the application will be refused (see EPO notice concerning application of Rules 49 and 50 EPC to handwritten amendments, OJ EPO 2013, 603).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to identify amendments and indicate basis (Rule 137(4) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever amendments are filed, the applicant must identify them and indicate the basis for them in the application as filed (Rule 137(4) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant fails to do so, the examining division may issue a communication under Rule 137(4) EPC requesting correction within a non‑extendable period of one month. Failure to reply within that period may lead to the application being deemed withdrawn under Article 94(4) EPC. See Guidelines for Examination, E‑IX,3.4 and H‑III,2.1/2.1.1 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of search results for priority applications (Rule 141(1) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each previous application whose priority is claimed, a copy of the search results produced by the authority with which the application was filed has to be supplied (Rule 141(1) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation applies to European patent applications and international applications filed on or after 1 January 2011. Cross the relevant box only if the copies are supplied when filing Form 1200. If the EPO includes a copy of the search results in the file, no action is required by the applicant (see OJ EPO 2016, A19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of the international application (language & content requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application was not published in an EPO official language, the applicant must furnish the EPO with a translation of that application within 31 months of the filing date or, where applicable, the (earliest) priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The translation must include the description, the claims as originally filed, any text in the drawings, and the abstract. It must also include indications under Rule 13bis.3 and 13bis.4 PCT for inventions relating to biological material and any published request for rectification (Rule 91.3(d) PCT). Proceedings in the European phase will be conducted in the language of the translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of the priority application or declaration (Rule 53(3) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Rule 53(3) EPC, applicants may be invited by the EPO to file a translation of the previous (priority) application, or they can submit a declaration that the European application is a complete translation of the previous application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A declaration under Rule 53(3) may be made by crossing the box in section 7.3 of Form 1200; if filed, no invitation to file a translation of the priority application will be issued (see OJ EPO 2013,150).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation must include claims amended under Article 19 PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant wishes subsequent proceedings to be based on the claims as amended under Article 19 PCT, the translation must also include those claims together with any explanatory statement and the accompanying letter under Rule 46.5(b) PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the amended claims and required statements/letters are included in the translation to have the proceedings based on the amended claims (see Rules 49.5(a)(ii), 49.5(c) and (c‑bis) PCT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations of IPER annexes where PCT Chapter II applies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where PCT Chapter II applies, applicants must prepare and file translations of all annexes to the international preliminary examination report (IPER), regardless of whether they seek protection for the same version of the application documents as was the subject of that report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement follows Article 36(2)(b) and (3)(b), Rule 70.16(a) PCT and Rule 74.1 PCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological material deposit information and receipt (Rules 13bis & 31 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: If biological material is involved, applicants should indicate the name and address of the depositary institution and the accession number of the deposited biological material in section 8 of Form 1200, and may specify the depositor's identification reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should indicate where in the description the Rule 31(1)(c) EPC information (depositary institution and accession number) can be found. To enable the EPO to check compliance, the receipt issued by the depositary institution is to be submitted to the EPO; applicants are strongly advised to submit the receipt when filing the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of undertaking to issue sample for biological material (Rule 33(1) & (2) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who are the depositor of the biological material may waive their right to an undertaking from the requester to issue a sample of the biological material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The waiver must be expressly declared to the EPO in a separate signed statement specifying the biological material (depositary institution and accession number or depositor's reference number as shown in the application documents). The waiver may be submitted at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings for nucleotide/amino acid disclosures (WIPO ST.25/ST.26; Rules 163(3) & 30(3) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application discloses nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences, a sequence listing in electronic form complying with the applicable WIPO standard (ST.25 or ST.26 depending on filing date) and the PCT Administrative Instructions must be available to the EPO as designated/elected Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a standardised electronic sequence listing is not available to the EPO, a standardised electronic listing must be filed on entry into the European phase; otherwise the EPO will invite the applicant to file it (Rule 163(3) EPC) and a late furnishing fee is payable. If submitted on entry, the applicant must declare (e.g. by crossing the box in section 9.2) that the listing does not include matter beyond the content of the application as originally filed. See decision of the President and notices (OJ EPO 2021, A96/A97) for filing details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of contracting states on entry (Article 79(1) EPC; Rule 4.9(a) PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: All contracting states designated in the international patent application and party to the EPC at the time of its filing are deemed to be designated on entry into the European phase (Article 79(1) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications entering the regional phase on or after 1 April 2009, payment of the flat‑rate designation fee covers all EPC contracting states unless individual designations are expressly withdrawn (Article 2, item 3, RFees). The EPC contracting states validly designated on entry are those specified in the international phase (Rule 4.9(a) PCT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension/validation and timing of payment (Rule 159(1)(d) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application and the European patent granted in respect of it may be extended or validated to non‑EPC contracting states designated for a national patent where extension/validation agreements were in force at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for extension/validation for a state is deemed withdrawn if the extension/validation fee is not paid to the EPO within the time limit laid down in the EPC for paying the designation fee (Rule 159(1)(d) EPC). The EPO publishes necessary information about such agreements in good time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for early processing (early entry) (Rule 159(1) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who wish the EPO to start processing an application before expiry of the 31‑month time limit under Rule 159(1) EPC must file an express request for early processing (cross box 12.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for early processing is effective on the date of its filing only if the Rule 159(1) EPC requirements applicable on that date have been complied with; the exact requirements depend on the filing date of the request (see OJ EPO 2013, 156). An effective early processing request terminates the international phase in respect of the EPO and the application will be processed immediately as a European application from that date; reversion to the 31‑month time limit is excluded. Consequently, time limits for filing the request for examination and paying the examination fee, designation fee and third renewal fee become those applying to a European application (i.e. not deferred to the 31‑month limit). Automatic debiting of relevant fees is available for requests filed on/after 1 Nov 2017 but only if documents referred to in Article 20 PCT are available to the EPO; otherwise applicants must pay the relevant fees on filing by other means or the request will take effect only when EPO receives the Article 20 documents from the IB (Rule 47.4 PCT). Applicants are recommended to read the relevant notice and Guidelines (E‑IX,2.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of communication under Rules 161 and 162 EPC to accelerate procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To accelerate the European grant procedure applicants can expressly waive their right to communications under Rules 161(1) or (2) and 162 EPC by crossing the first box in section 12.2 of the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPO will not issue the communication only if, in addition to the waiver, the applicant has on entry fulfilled all the requirements of Rules 161 and 162 EPC (i.e. payment of any claims fees due and, where required, submission of a response under Rule 161(1) EPC) so that the application can proceed directly to the supplementary European search or to examination. Applicants may also request accelerated search or examination under PACE. If the right to communication has not been validly waived, the communication will be issued and the application processed only after expiry of the six‑month period, even if a PACE request has been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of invitation under Rule 70(2) EPC
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who file the request for examination before receiving the supplementary European search report can waive their right to be asked for confirmation under Rule 70(2) EPC by crossing the second box in section 12.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If waived, confirmation is deemed given when the supplementary European search report is transmitted to them. With regard to the legal consequences, see Guidelines for Examination, C‑VI,3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment methods and fee information
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees due in respect of a patent application can be paid by debiting a deposit account, by credit card or by bank transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details: debiting a deposit account/automatic debiting procedures are set out in the Arrangements for deposit accounts (ADA) and Arrangements for the automatic debiting procedure (AAD) and related notices; careful attention should be paid to conditions for filing debit orders. Credit card payments must be made via the EPO's credit card fee payment service using accepted cards (as of Dec 2017: MasterCard and VISA). Bank transfer procedures and account details (Commerzbank AG, IBAN DE20 7008 0000 0333 8800 00, BIC DRESDEFF700) are published in the Official Journal. For fee amounts, consult the 'Schedule of fees and expenses' or the 'Interactive schedule of fees' on the EPO website; see also 'Guidance for the payment of fees, costs and prices' in the Official Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 1200 table for section 6 – additional fee calculation (Form 1200.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The table for section 6 of Form 1200.3 is used for calculating the additional fee for applications comprising more than 35 pages (Article 2, item 1a, RFees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must specify in the table on page 8 of Form 1200 the documents to be used for the European phase, which form the basis for calculation of any additional fee; any exceptional circumstances needing further explanation must be clarified on an additional sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of test reports from IPEA proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has supplied test reports in proceedings before the EPO as International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA), the EPO assumes that it may also use them in the European grant proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further action is required to permit the EPO to use such reports, but applicants should be aware the EPO may rely on them in examination.
